#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This Pull Request prevents users from sending a space-prefixed bearer tokens, e.g.:

```
$ curl -k https://IP -H "Authorization: Bearer  asdf"
```

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #106142

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The space-prefixed Authorization headers violate [RFC 6750, Section 2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Bearer tokens prefixed with a space are not allowed due to RFC 6750, Section 2.1 violation
```

issue_context.title: kube-apiserver incorrectly parses tokens starting with ' '
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

kube-apiserver authenticated the token " TOKEN" as `system:anonymous` (note the leading space).

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-apiserver should reject the invalid authorization header.

The bearer token [RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1) specifies a single space between "Bearer" and the token value.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
$ IP=<address of kube-apiserver>
$ curl -k https://IP -H "Authorization: Bearer asdf"
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {
    
  },
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "Unauthorized",
  "reason": "Unauthorized",
  "code": 401
}
$ curl -k https://IP -H "Authorization: Bearer  asdf"
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {
    
  },
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "forbidden: User \"system:anonymous\" cannot get path \"/\"",
  "reason": "Forbidden",
  "details": {
    
  },
  "code": 403
}
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

I think the correct behavior here would be to fail the request as unauthorized.  However, that is technically a breaking change since a (poorly coded) client could be currently sending an invalid token and falling through to the anonymous user (and if said client is doing something like healthz checks, they will likely not notice anything is wrong).

We will reach out on the SIG Auth ML to see if anyone is concerned about us making this breaking change.
We can start with a warning and maybe a metric. We can consider treating this as a bug sometime down the line, but just warning that we are falling through to anonymous seems reasonable and useful.
@enj Should we start off with a warning message and decide later if we want to change the default behavior?

> @enj Should we start off with a warning message and decide later if we want to change the default behavior?

Yeah that seems reasonable to me.
@SataQiu Are you still looking at this issue? If not, I can open a PR to add the warning.
/assign

According to the [RFC 6750, Section 2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1), the Authorization Request Header is structured as the following:

> b64token    = 1*( ALPHA / DIGIT /
>                       "-" / "." / "_" / "~" / "+" / "/" ) *"="
>     credentials = "Bearer" 1*SP b64token

This means, that " TOKEN" is simply invalid. I proposed a Pull Request (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109558) with a fix that treats this case an invalid header. 

In our testsuite, I have also seen cases, where we allow string after the token (see the `TestAuthenticateRequestIncludingValueAfterToken`). I wonder why we are doing this?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114165 just reported this also impacts behavior of TokenReview, which delegates to the authentication chain
Same, I just stumbled upon this problem. I was never expecting this behavior and I couldn't find references to this anywhere. My report: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114165

Some next steps for this could include:

If a request is made with a bearer token with a leading space _and_ that request is successfully authorized:

1. Increment a metric
2. Add an audit annotation
3. Add a debug log statement

This should be enough for cluster admins to see if they have misconfigured clients.  At some future point we could make leading spaces into an error.

@enj I like the visibility that you propose but also as a developer, I would want to trust that the Kubernetes API is properly authorizing tokens. My team and myself struggled for days trying to understand where we went wrong. We were always getting `authorized: true` and `system:anonymous` until we finally noticed that leading space. We should at the very least document the behavior for others to know.
This issue is the tracking document for the bug.  I am unaware of any other place we would put this information.

This issue has not been updated in over 1 year, and should be re-triaged.
